superposition

**Identity / target / source:** `ai:superposition` → `ai-superposition` → `src/demos/ai/ai-superposition`; source `company/domains/proposals/2026-10-18-ai-map-expansion.json#concepts/155`; brief `company/domains/briefs/2026-10-19-ai-next30e.md#26-superposition`. **Packet:** I2. **Level / prerequisites:** stretch; `ai:polysemantic-neurons`, `ai:cosine-similarity`.

**Nearest / distinct payoff:** polysemantic-neurons gives one ambiguous coordinate; this embeds three sparse feature directions in2D and computes recoverability/interference as co-occurrence changes.

**Computed primary model:** Three unit vectorsvA=(1,0),vB=(−.5,sqrt3/2),vC=(−.5,−sqrt3/2). Encode nonnegative activationsa byz=sum a_i*v_i; readout_i=ReLU(v_i dotz). Single activeA amplitude1 decodes[1,0,0] exactly. CoactiveA+B givesz=(.5,sqrt3/2), raw dots[.5,.5,−1], decoded[.5,.5,0], attenuating both true amplitudes1.

**Countercase / boundary:** All three active sum toz0 and decode[0,0,0], indistinguishable from no active features. Sparsity enables this particular singleton recovery but arbitrary dense patterns are not uniquely recoverable. This supplied geometry is not a learned phase transition, unique semantic decomposition or full reconstruction guarantee.

**Prediction / transfer recall:** Predict whether three coactive directions remain distinct in2D; recall every singleton decodes exactly while a pair’s recovered amplitudes need not stay1.

**Intervention / retained witness:** Activate one/two/three features computes actual vector sum, dot readouts and reconstruction error. Retain singleton recovery and dense cancellation together; no merely decorative direction diagram. Keep amplitude error distinct from binary support detection.

**Source obligation:** [Elhage et al. original Toy Models PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2209.10652), opened2026-10-19, “Definitions and Motivation” and toy ReLU embedding/unembedding setup. Only the local constructed activations/directions below are admitted; the paper’s trained phase transitions, real-model prevalence and semantic feature identities are not reproduced.
